headline: Trade beat and a firmer stock market trim the rally; 10Y CCDC up 0.9bp to 1.597%
summary: CGBs eased for a second day as profit-taking met stronger October trade data and a broad rally in Shenzhen and ChiNext shares. The CCDC 10-year rose 0.9bp to 1.597% and the 30-year 0.8bp to 2.036%, with the 7–10Y sector leading the sell-off while the 2- and 5-year rose only about 0.5bp, and futures fell across the strip (TL −0.22%, T −0.08%). Policy banks matched CGBs at 10Y and the long end (CDB 10-year +1.0bp to about 1.647%, spread 5.0bp) but lagged again at 3–5Y, where CDB 5-year rose 1.3bp and its spread widened 0.9bp to 12.4bp; ADBC and EXIM 10-year rose 0.8bp.
drivers: October exports rose 35.2% y/y (forecast 33.5%, prior 36.3%) and imports 41.6% (forecast 32%, prior 31%), the fastest import growth in five years, on chips, copper and energy. The surplus narrowed to $105.3bn but topped $1tn year-to-date, a reminder that external demand is strong and gave traders another reason to bank gains near record-low yields.

Funds were heavy net sellers of bonds in the first week of November, mostly credit, and brokers sold long rate bonds into the rally, per Cailian data. With the 10-year still about 1bp above Friday's 1-year low and the PBOC shrinking its 3-month outright repos, traders expect a period of consolidation rather than a reversal.

The Shanghai Composite edged up 0.08% but the Shenzhen index rose 0.86% and ChiNext 1.46%, with about 4,270 stocks up and turnover of about RMB1.5tn, which cooled the haven bid. The PBOC fixed the yuan stronger at about 6.717 per dollar and onshore yuan traded near 6.67.
PBOC turns to a small injection

The PBOC ran RMB190bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% against RMB182bn maturing, a RMB8bn net injection that ended six days of drains. Overnight Shibor rose 0.9bp to 1.323% while 7-day slipped 0.7bp to 1.354%, so funding stayed close to the anchor and the front end held up best; EXIM's 1-year cleared at 1.27% with 3.1 times cover.
data: Oct trade (Nov 10)
Strong external demand and import growth trim the growth-scare case for bonds and triggered mild profit-taking.
Oct PPI (Nov 9)
Energy-driven cost push that squeezes margins rather than signalling demand; bonds looked through it.
Oct CPI (Nov 9)
Soft household demand keeps the easing bias intact and supports low long-end yields.
Oct FX reserves (Nov 7)
$3.405tn (f $3.41tn, p $3.400tn); gold +0.83m oz, 24th month of buying
Stable reserves and a strong yuan year-to-date leave the PBOC room to keep funding cheap.
Oct RatingDog services PMI (Nov 4)
50.8 (f 51.5, p 51.6); composite 52.0 (p 52.4); selling prices cut for a 2nd month
Slowest services growth since July with falling prices supports low yields.
Oct RatingDog mfg PMI (Nov 2)
52.0 (f 51.6, p 52.1); output fastest since April; 11th month of expansion
Export-facing firms are holding up, which tempers the weak official print but did not stop the bond rally.
Oct official PMIs (Oct 31)
Mfg 49.3 (f 50.0, p 50.1); new orders 49.4; non-mfg 49.7 (p 50.2); composite 49.7
Back in contraction with softer prices, which supports low yields and continued easy funding.
view: Neutral leaning long for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.56–1.62% CCDC range. Strong trade data and firmer stocks argue for a pause after the anchor-switch rally, but core inflation is cooling, the 1.25% overnight anchor holds funding near 1.3%, and insurers and banks usually start year-end buying of long bonds from mid-November, so dips should be bought rather than sold. I keep the 10-year buy level at 1.61–1.62%, the 5Y-into-10Y switch, the underweight in policy banks against CGBs at 10Y and the long end, and the preference for ADBC/EXIM over CDB. Strong October credit and activity data or a sustained equity rally would push the 10-year to 1.62%, while weak credit data or a liquidity injection around the mid-November tax period could take it back to 1.56%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year rose 0.5bp to 1.221%, still at its 1-year low (1st percentile, average 1.306%), and the 1-year rose 1.1bp to 1.177%. The PBOC added a net RMB8bn after six days of drains and overnight Shibor rose 0.9bp to 1.323%, so funding sits just above the 1.25% anchor and the front end has little room left.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: 2s5s10s fell 0.5bp to −19.8bp, a new 1-year rich extreme (0th percentile, average −7.8bp), as the 5-year rose only 0.4bp to 1.310% while the 10-year rose 0.9bp. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is at 28.7bp (71st percentile, average 26.5bp), about flat on entry and inside the 31bp stop; 5s7s10s is −6.9bp (12th percentile).
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year rose 0.9bp to 1.597%, 1bp above its 1-year low, so the 1.61–1.62% buy level has not been reached. Against neighbours it still screens cheap: 7s10s20s is −24.7bp, about the 81st percentile against a −29.4bp average.
buckets.call: Buy 10-year CGBs on a back-up to 1.61–1.62%, target 1.57%, stop 1.645%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year rose 0.8bp to 2.036% and 10s30s is 44.0bp, about the 31st percentile against a 45.8bp average. 30s50s widened 0.3bp to 12.0bp (6th percentile); seasonal insurer demand from mid-November and only two 30-year reopenings left support the block, but the spread cushion is thin.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 5.0bp over CGB (18th percentile, average 9.7bp), so the switch from ~3bp is about 2bp in the money. Policy banks lagged again at 3–5Y, where CDB 5-year widened 0.9bp to 12.4bp (27th percentile), while the 2-year spread of 11.8bp stays near its 1-year tight (2nd percentile).
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 3.2bp more than CDB (74th percentile, average 1.3bp) and EXIM 2.2bp (60th percentile, average 2.0bp), both 0.2bp tighter today. The pickup reflects heavy tap supply rather than credit, and auction demand stays firm, with EXIM's 1-year drawing 3.1 times cover.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 4.9bp over CGB, at its 1-year low (0th percentile, average 10.5bp), and the 30-year 11.0bp, also at its 1-year tight (average 12.6bp). Long policy bank bonds rose 0.8bp, exactly in line with CGBs, leaving no cushion if supply picks up.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.
